data.title: Scienture’s Arbli and Rezenopy Growth Supports Positive Outlook; $6 Price Target Reaffirmed
data.description:
Analyst Naz Rahman of Maxim Group reiterated a Buy rating on Scienture Holdings, retaining the price target of $6.00.

Naz Rahman’s rating is based on Scienture’s growing commercial opportunity in Arbli and Rezenopy, two products addressing specialized medical needs. Third-quarter revenue exceeded expectations and rose sharply after Rezenopy’s launch, while its early contribution suggests meaningful demand and access to roughly 60% of the institutional market.
Arbli’s reported sales were affected by rebate and discount accruals, but prescription volume, wholesale units, and new-patient additions continued to increase, with coverage now extending to more than 100 million lives. With cash resources and receivables considered sufficient to support the business toward profitability, Rahman views future reimbursement gains and improved Arbli revenue recognition as catalysts; the $6 price target remains unchanged.

data.title: Kazia Therapeutics: Buy Rating Maintained Despite Price-Target Cut to $20 on Paxalisib Promise
data.description:
Maxim Group analyst Naz Rahman has reiterated their bullish stance on KZIA stock, giving a Buy rating on November 3.

Naz Rahman’s rating is based on several factors, led by encouraging clinical evidence for paxalisib in advanced triple-negative breast cancer. In a small Phase 1b data set, most evaluable patients responded or maintained stable disease, while treatment also appeared to improve biological markers associated with resistance and metastasis. The drug’s tolerability, including the absence of serious or severe treatment-related toxicities reported in the update, further supports its potential risk-reward profile.

Paxalisib is also being studied in other cancers and rare diseases, creating additional opportunities beyond the analyst’s current valuation model. Kazia’s cash position, recent financing, milestone income, and potential warrant proceeds are expected to support operations for several years, while multiple 2027 data releases could provide important catalysts. Although new shares reduced Rahman’s price target from $30 to $20, he maintained the Buy rating because of paxalisib’s potential to become a leading therapy in its class and the company’s meaningful upcoming clinical milestones.

In another report released on November 3, Canaccord Genuity also maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a $29.00 price target.

data.title: Rezolute Buy Rating Supported by Positive ersodetug Data and $14 Price Target
data.description:
Jason McCarthy, an analyst from Maxim Group, maintained the Buy rating on Rezolute. The associated price target remains the same with $14.00.

Jason McCarthy’s rating is based on several factors, led by encouraging preliminary results from Rezolute’s Phase 3 upLIFT study of ersodetug in tumor hyperinsulinism. Twelve of 13 evaluable patients were able to stop intravenous glucose, and the current responder tally appears to exceed the threshold needed for statistical success when the complete 16-patient analysis is released. A positive outcome could support FDA discussions on biologics applications for both tumor and congenital hyperinsulinism.

Rezolute also has a potential path for congenital hyperinsulinism through durable open-label extension results, ongoing glycemic control, reduced background-treatment use, and an FDA indication to seek a pre-BLA meeting despite earlier trial endpoint misses. In addition, a $100 million financing alongside existing cash is expected to extend operations into the second half of 2028 and help fund commercialization. These catalysts support the Buy view, while the price target remains unchanged at $14.

In another report released on November 17, Wedbush also assigned a Buy rating to the stock with a $10.00 price target.

RZLT’s price has also changed moderately for the past six months – from $3.240 to $4.250, which is a 31.17% increase.

data.title: Vyome’s VT-1953 Shows Promise in Malignant Wounds; Analyst Maintains $15 Price Target
data.description:
Analyst Jason McCarthy of Maxim Group maintained a Buy rating on Vyome Holdings, retaining the price target of $15.00.

Jason McCarthy’s rating is based on VT-1953’s promising clinical profile and substantial unmet need in malignant fungating wounds, where no FDA-approved treatments currently exist. The therapy produced statistically meaningful reductions in wound malodor and lesion pain in a Phase 2 study, supporting its potential as the company’s main value driver and a possible pivotal Phase 3 program after further FDA discussions.
Vyome also retains longer-term upside from VT-1908 for anterior uveitis and its early-stage JAK inhibitor portfolio, with recent patent progress strengthening pipeline optionality. The company’s $6.9 million cash balance, expected runway into the second half of 2027, and additional ATM capacity support continued development, while the $15 price target remains unchanged.

HIND’s price has also changed moderately for the past six months – from $1.890 to $1.510, which is a -20.11% drop .

data.title: Euroseas’ Strong Charter Rates and Shipping Outlook Support Buy Rating; $94 Price Target Reiterated
data.description:
Tate Sullivan, an analyst from Maxim Group, reiterated the Buy rating on Euroseas. The associated price target remains the same with $94.00.

Tate Sullivan has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, including Euroseas’ stronger-than-expected third-quarter time charter equivalent rate and favorable outlook for shipping demand. He expects China’s expanding imports of coal, bauxite, and iron ore to support dry-bulk activity, while exports of electric vehicles, industrial equipment, and smartphones should create additional demand for containerships.
Euroseas also offers improving shareholder returns, highlighted by a 6.3% quarterly dividend increase and a 5.5% yield, with further growth anticipated. data.title: Simon Property Group’s Strong Momentum and Leasing Pipeline Support Buy Rating; $260 Target Maintained
data.description:
Caitlin Burrows, an analyst from Goldman Sachs, maintained the Buy rating on Simon Property. The associated price target remains the same with $260.00.

Caitlin Burrows’s rating is based on Simon Property Group’s strong operating momentum and favorable leasing backdrop. Domestic property NOI rose 7.3% year to date through the third quarter of 2026, supported by Taubman margin gains, better occupancy, higher rents, overage income, and redevelopment. The planned replacement of Saks Off 5th space should further enhance future earnings as the re-leased area is expected to generate substantially higher rent.

Management also reported a leasing pipeline up about 30% year over year, indicating retailers continue to seek space and giving Simon scope to improve its tenant mix. Stable luxury demand, resilient consumers, and healthy mall traffic could support sales and provide upside to guidance, while the company sees AI-driven leisure spending as an additional tailwind. Against this backdrop, Burrows maintained the Buy rating and left the price target unchanged at $260.

In another report released on November 15, Bank of America Securities also reiterated a Buy rating on the stock with a $260.00 price target.
